title: Maximum Beauty of an Array After Applying Operation
summary: Given an array nums and a non-negative integer k, you can perform an operation on each index once to replace the element with any integer within k of its original value.
statement: Given an array nums and a non-negative integer k, you can perform an operation on each index once to replace the element with any integer within k of its original value. The goal is to maximize the length of the longest subsequence of equal elements. Return the maximum possible beauty of the array after performing these operations.
constraints: Each value may independently be replaced by any integer within k of itself.
Beauty is the greatest achievable frequency of one common resulting value.
hints: Two values can reach a common target exactly when their k-radius intervals overlap.
After sorting, a feasible group has maximum minus minimum at most 2k.
Use a sliding window and shrink while its span exceeds 2k.
For one-dimensional equal-radius intervals, the extremes overlap iff every interval shares a common point.
editorial: For one-dimensional equal-radius intervals, the extremes overlap iff every interval shares a common point.

tests.explanation: Values one, two, and four can all become a common value, giving beauty three.
